title: Sample 12-7: Word List in a Sidebar

illustrates.quote: When a sidebar is necessary for the understanding of a particular text, insert that sidebar before the related text. (See Sample 12-7: Word List in a Sidebar on page 12-12.)

blocks.features: White text on a red banner with a large numeral '6'.

blocks.title: Chapter Summary
blocks.features: Boxed sidebar with a yellow banner title, spanning the width of the page above the vocabulary exercise.
Each item begins with a bold 'Lesson N' label followed by a bullet, then the lesson's summary sentence(s).

items.text: Violence is a serious public health problem in the United States. You can help to prevent violence in your community.
To prevent violent situations and make your school a safe place, avoid weapons and gangs and deal with bullies in a healthful way.
Knowing and practicing safe habits can help you prevent unintentional injuries at home, outdoors, and on the road.
Identifying severe weather conditions and natural disasters and being aware of the safety measures for each type of weather emergency will help you avoid unintentional injuries.
Being skilled in first aid procedures will prepare you to respond in a medical emergency. These skills will also enable you to take safe actions to reduce your risk of illness or injury.

blocks.features: White text on an orange banner; confirmed CENTRED (12 leading blank cells, matching floor((40-15)/2)=12 for its own 15-cell braille text ',use ,vocabul>y') by forward-translating this heading and matching byte-for-byte against the given braille line 1.

blocks.text: Choose the correct term from the list to complete each sentence.

blocks.features: Numbered fill-in-the-blank sentences; each blank is a printed underscore rule (escaped here as \_ so Emboss's cell-markup DSL does not read the run as an <u>underline</u> toggle -- Emboss has no dot-5 blank-fill mechanism at all, F-36, so this is expected to mismatch either way).

items.text: If a material is able to catch fire easily, it is \_\_\_\_\_\_.
A physical attack or the threat of a physical attack is an example of \_\_\_\_\_\_.
A group of people who are often involved in illegal and violent activities is a(n) \_\_\_\_\_\_.
A dangerous reduction in blood flow within the body is \_\_\_\_\_\_.
The killing of one person by another person is \_\_\_\_\_\_.
A condition in which the body's temperature falls significantly below normal is \_\_\_\_\_\_.
An overheating of the body that is life-threatening is \_\_\_\_\_\_.
A mild burn that affects the first, or outer layer of the skin, causing pain, redness, and swelling is a(n) \_\_\_\_\_\_.

print.notes: This sample illustrates rule 12.3.1g: the word-list sidebar is necessary for understanding the fill-in-the-blank sentences that follow, so it is inserted immediately BEFORE that related text (matching its own print position here, unlike Sample 12-3 where the sidebar's braille position is moved to follow an arrow). The braille excerpt (source .txt lines 10188-10206, PDF p.353) begins only at the 'Use Vocabulary' heading -- the 'Chapter 6 Review' heading and the entire 'Chapter Summary' sidebar (all five lesson summaries) have no braille counterpart anywhere in this excerpt, with no omission marker of any kind at that point (unlike Sample 12-3's two explicit '444' markers). The braille also transcribes only the first 2 of the print's 8 fill-in-the-blank sentences, ending in a '444' omission marker.
print.printFeatures: A chapter-review page: a red 'Chapter 6 Review' banner, a yellow-bannered 'Chapter Summary' sidebar spanning the full width, an orange-bannered 'Use Vocabulary' section with a boxed word-list sidebar to the left of eight numbered fill-in-the-blank sentences, and the print page number 'C78' at bottom left.

braille.notes: 19 lines (source .txt lines 10188-10206). Line 1 is the CENTRED heading 'Use Vocabulary' (12 leading blank cells, matching floor((40-15)/2)=12 for its own 15-cell braille text ',use ,vocabul>y' -- not a fixed cell-5 indent), ending with the print page number 'C78' in braille (,c#gh). Lines 3-4 are the directions line, both at a fixed 4-cell margin (matching BANA's attribution/directions convention, not an ordinary 3-1 paragraph). Lines 6-13 are the eight vocabulary terms, flush left, with NO top or bottom box-line border anywhere around them -- the print's own word-list sidebar is transcribed here as plain inserted text, not a boxed sidebar (see resolution: this is a genuine Emboss gap, F-230). Lines 15-18 are the first two of the print's eight fill-in-the-blank sentences; line 19 is a literal '444' omission marker, both runs dropped it and recorded a blank line instead (corrected here directly against the source .txt and the rendered PDF page image, p.353, which shows it as the excerpt's own numbered line 19).

uncertain: The heading 'Chapter 6 Review' and the 'Chapter Summary' sidebar's own 'Lesson N' items have no braille counterpart anywhere in this excerpt (not even an omission marker); their exact braille formatting (whether boxed, and at what margin) cannot be verified from this source.
resolution: Run B's braille.lines were empty for this file (an apparent extraction failure in that run); run A's 19-line transcription is used, corrected against the source .txt and the rendered PDF page image (p.353) exactly as for Sample 12-3: line 19, a literal '444' omission marker in the source, was recorded as a blank line by run A and is restored here. Print.blocks records the FULL print content, including the 'Chapter 6 Review' heading and the entire 'Chapter Summary' sidebar that this braille excerpt omits with no marker at all (per the section-7 sample-7-03 precedent for an unmarked print/braille length mismatch in the source corpus) and the full 8-item fill-in-the-blank list (per the section-3 sample-3-01 / section-7 sample-7-03 precedent for a '444'-marked truncation) rather than the 2 items the braille actually transcribes -- buildModel12 is expected to over-produce at both points, a documented excerpt limitation, not an Emboss defect. The vocabulary word-list sidebar itself is a genuine new finding: BANA 12.3.1f treats box lines as being added only 'for clarity if the content of the sidebar interrupts the flow of text', implying they are conditional, but this sample's own braille shows a sidebar transcribed with NO box-line border at all (plain inserted text, blank line before and after per 12.3.1e) -- Emboss's `formatBox` (shared by every 'box'/'sidebar' document-model block) unconditionally emits top and bottom border lines with no way to omit them, so buildModel12's box-based rendering of this sidebar is expected to mismatch on that account; recorded as new finding F-230.
